C. 55M 1 38
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.    File No............
Section 1, Special Branch Station,    8640
REPORT
Date August 16, 19 38.
Subject Local National Salvation Elements promote "Thrift Society".
Made by D.S. McKeown    Forwarded by [Signature]

Instructions are respectfully requested for the disposal
of the remaining two prisoners now in custody at the Chengtu
Road Station connected with the promotion of a "Thrift "
movement as a cloak to further the anti-Japanese boycott
movement.

The following is a summary of the evidence against these
two persons:-

(1) Chiang Wen-kwei (蒋文桂), one of the leaders of the
movement, admits being assigned by the Communist Party
to investigate and report the labour situation in the
Commercial Press. A preparatory member of the Communist
Party. Secret communist publication entitled "Truth
(真言 )" found in his home. "Knowledge for new party
members," and 27 other kinds of anti-Japanese and leftist
literature. One of the publishers of the magazine entitled
"Long Hwa (Wave)", a secret publication previously unknown,
containing national salvation propaganda. Responsible
for distribution of the magazine "Unity" among the workers
of the Commercial Press. Also served as purchasing agent
for anti-Japanese and Communist books published in Hankow.

(2) Soong Hsi-vung(宋希文): A member of the "Thrift Society"
Attended two secret meetings. Arranged for the printing
of 60 copies of a handbill bearing on the "Thrift move-
ment," national salvation in nature. Implicated by Tsang
Hei-ngoch as a promoter of the "After Office Hours
Reading Society," which according to Chiang Wen Kwei was
to promote the National Salvation movement. Introduced
one member to the "Thrift Society."

（左侧批注：D.S. McKeown 17/8）
（左侧批注：Deport）
（印章：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE 17 AUG. 1938）
（底部手写：S.B.? 17/8）

报告
日期：1938年8月16日。
主题：本地救国分子鼓吹“节约社”。
制作人：D.S. McKeown    转呈人 [签名]

现恭敬地请求指示，以处置目前羁押在成都路分局、与鼓吹“节约”运动有关的两名剩余囚犯，该运动实为掩护进一步开展抵制日货运动。

以下是针对此二人的证据摘要：-

(1) 蒋文桂（蒋文桂），该运动的领导人之一，承认受共产党指派调查并报告商务印书馆的劳工情况。其为共产党预备党员。在其家中搜获名为《真言》的秘密共产党刊物。《新党员知识》及其他27种反日和左翼文献。他是此前不为人知的秘密刊物《龙华（Wave）》的出版商之一，该刊物包含救国宣传内容。负责在商务印书馆工人中分发《团结》杂志。还担任汉口出版的反日和共产党书籍的采购代理。

(2) 宋希文（宋希文）：“节约社”成员。参加了两次秘密会议。安排印刷了60份涉及“节约运动”的传单，性质属于救国。被曾黑哥（Tsang Hei-ngoch，音译）指认为“业余读书会”的鼓吹者，据蒋文桂称，该会旨在推动救国运动。向“节约社”介绍了一名成员。

（左侧批注：D.S. McKeown 17/8）
（左侧批注：驱逐）
（印章：上海公共租界工部局警务处处长办公室 1938年8月17日）
（底部手写：S.B.? 17/8）

page_data.en:
TRANSLATION OF A PETITION SUBMITTED BY WONG KYING-
FOH (王金福), BROTHER OF WONG KYING-DAO (王景陶)
( IN CUSTODY ). WONG KYING-FOH IS A NATIVE OF
SHANGHAI, FORMERLY RESIDING AT 11 WONG KA ZAH,
WEST PAOSHENG ROAD, CHAPEI, AND AT PRESENT LIVING
AT NO. 345 HUH DAH LI, RUE BOURGEAT.

I beg to state that Wong Kying-dao (王景陶),
a iae King Dau (金桃), is my younger brother, age 21.
After graduating from the Footung Primary School (浦东小学),
he attended the Ming Jang Middle School, North Paoshing
Road, Chapei, and completed his course in the junior mid-
dle school in 1935. During his study in that school, he
was a favourite student of his school-master Dr. R.J. Bryan
who has returned to the U.S.A. He is very diligent and
honest, and is a member of the Baptist Church. He continued
to study in the Ming Jang School until the outbreak of the
August 13th incident, when the institute closed. The master
was then Mr. James Hamilton Ware.

My brother then joined the Chien Chwang Middle
School, 318 Weihaiwei Road in order to complete his middle
school course. He graduated this summer, and decided to
receive an advanced course. Owing to financial difficulties,
he, on the information of his school-mates, and being a
Christian, applied to the Church Office at Yuen Ming Yuen
Road, for monetary assistance. His request was approved
with the recommendation of the principal of the Ming Jang
Middle School certifying that he is of good behavior and
excellent education. Consequently he started to refresh
his mind of his old lessons and used to apply to the
teachers of the Chien Chwang Middle School for assistance
in solving difficult problems.

On July 24 (Sunday), at about 8 a.m., my brother
left for the Chien Chwang School, carrying with him a
physics book, with the intention of asking his teacher to
explain some problems relating to physics. The teacher
was absent, so my brother remained on the premises and
page_data.zh:
王金福（WONG KYING-FOH）提交的请愿书译文，王金福系在押人员王景陶（WONG KYING-DAO）之兄。王金福系上海人，原住闸北宝兴西路王家宅11号，现住布尔热路胡达里345号。

谨呈者，王景陶（又名金桃），系舍弟，年21岁。自浦东小学毕业后，入读闸北宝兴北路明强中学，并于1935年完成初中课程。在该校就读期间，深得该校校长R.J. Bryan博士喜爱，Bryan博士已返回美国。他勤奋诚实，且为浸信会教友。八一三事变爆发、学校停办前，他一直就读于明强中学。当时的校长是James Hamilton Ware先生。

随后，舍弟转入威海卫路318号坚庄中学，以完成其中学课程。他于今年夏季毕业，并决定进修高级课程。由于经济困难，经同学告知，且身为基督徒，他向圆明园路教会办事处申请经济援助。其请求获准，并附有明强中学校长出具的证明书，证实其品行端正、学业优良。因此，他开始温习旧课，并常向坚庄中学的老师请教疑难问题。

7月24日（星期日）上午8时许，舍弟携带一本物理课本前往坚庄中学，意在请老师讲解一些物理方面的问题。因老师不在，舍弟便留在校园内，

page_data.en:
- 2 -
read newspapers to await the return of the physics teacher.
At about 9.30 a.m., he was arrested in a class
room without any reason to his knowledge. (The above
information was obtained from a servant of the Chien
Chwang Middle School.)
My brother was not acquainted with any persons
who attended during the meeting, and I believe that this
point has been brought to your notice. He has never joined
any public bodies or participated in the formation of any
organizations. He was seldom out except going to school
(this can be proved by our neighbours). He is quite a good
person and it appears to be a mistake to arrest him.
Subsequent to his arrest, my mother has been
very uneasy. She partakes of only a little food, and is
nearly in a state of mental disorder. She simply hopes for
the return of her son.
I herewith submitted a petition together with
a letter of Mr. James Hamilton Ware, principal of the Ming
Jang Middle School to certify that Wong Kying-foh is a
peaceful man and beg you to release him forthwith.

(chopped) Wong Kying-foh.
August 2, 1938.

阅读报纸，等候物理老师回来。
上午9时30分左右，他在教室里无故被捕（他对被捕原因毫不知情）。（上述信息得自坚庄中学的一名仆役。）
舍弟并不认识会议期间的任何出席者，我相信这一点已引起阁下的注意。他从未加入任何公共团体或参与组建任何组织。除上学外，他很少外出（此点可由我们的邻居证明）。他为人甚好，逮捕他似乎是个错误。
自他被捕后，家母一直非常不安。她进食极少，精神几近失常。她只盼儿子归来。
现随函提交请愿书一份，并附上明强中学校长James Hamilton Ware先生的信函，以证明王景陶（注：此处英文原文误写为王金福，根据上下文及中文请愿书内容应为王景陶）乃安分守己之人，恳请阁下立即将其释放。

（盖章）王金福。
1938年8月2日。

Transcript of a letter addressed to Foreign Detective i/c
Chengtu Road Police Station from Mr. Wang Lu Ngou, Attorney-
at-law.
------------------------------
Envelope:- To Foreign Det. Inspector,
           Chengtu Road Police Station.

From Wang Lu Ngou, Attorney-at-law,
     26 Avenue Joffre, corner of Rue
     Chapsal, A.J. or Room No. 524 Con-
     tinental Building, Nanking Road,
     Tel. No. 91088.

Letter:-

To Foreign Det. Inspector i/c Chengtu Road Stn.

Sir,

    The following is the verbal complaint made by my client
Chiang Lok Szi-

    "My son Chiang Vung Kwei, has been employed by the Commer-
cial Press for the past 5 years. His conduct is always good
and his movements are very quiet. On the 14-7-38, he was
arrested on Wei Hai Wei Road, but up to the present, he has
not yet been released. Being in old age, my subsistance is
entirely to depend upon my son, and my present livelihood is
rather depressed. In view of the foregoing, I implore you
to write a letter to the Foreign Det. Inspector i/c Chengtu
Road Station requesting the latter to have my son released on
security, to enable him (my son) to carry on his work as well
as to enable the whole family to avoid starvation".

    In view of the above, I hereby write you this letter,
with the request that you will allow the said Chiang Vung
Kwei to be released upon furnishing shop security.

                                    I remain,

                                    Yours faithfully,

                                    Wang Lu Ngou,
                                    Attorney-at-law.
                                    2-8-38.

信封：- 致外籍侦探督察，
           成都路捕房。

寄件人：律师王鲁五（Wang Lu Ngou，音译），
     霞飞路26号，查普萨尔路（Rue Chapsal）转角，A.J. 或南京路大陆大楼524室，
     电话：91088。

信件：-

致成都路捕房外籍侦探主管。

先生，

以下是我的当事人蒋洛士（Chiang Lok Szi，音译）的口述投诉——

“吾儿蒋永贵（Chiang Vung Kwei，音译）受雇于商务印书馆已五年。其行为一向良好，行踪非常低调。1938年7月14日，他在威海卫路被捕，但至今尚未获释。因余年事已高，生计完全依赖吾儿，目前生活颇为困顿。鉴于上述情况，恳请阁下致函成都路捕房外籍侦探主管，请求后者准予吾儿具保释放，使其（吾儿）能继续工作，并使全家免于饥饿。”

鉴于上述情况，特此致函，请求准予上述蒋永贵提供铺保后释放。

                                    此致，

                                    谨启，

                                    王鲁五（Wang Lu Ngou，音译），
                                    律师。
                                    1938年8月2日。

Translation of a letter addressed to Foreign Detective i/c
Chengtu Road Police Station from Mr. Wang Lu Ngou, Attorney-
at-law.
--------------------------
Envelope:- To Foreign Det. Inspector,
Chengtu Road Police Station.

From Wang Lu Ngou, Attorney-at-law,
26 Avenue Joffre, corner of Rue
Chapsel, F.C. or Room No. 524 Con-
tinental Building, Nanking Road,
Tel. No. 91980.

Letter:-

To Foreign Det. Inspector i/c Chengtu Road Stn.

Sir,

The following is the verbal complaint made by my client
Chiang Lok Sz:-

"My son Chiang Vung Kwei, has been employed by the Commer-
cial Press for the past 5 years. His conduct is always good
and his movements are very quiet. On the 24-7-38, he was
arrested on Wei Hai Wei Road, but up to the present, he has
not yet been released. Being in old age, my subsistance is
entirely to depend upon my son, and my present livelihood is
rather depressed. In view of the foregoing, I implore you
to write a letter to the Foreign Det. Inspector i/c Chengtu
Road Station requesting the latter to have my son released on
security, to enable him (my son) to carry on his work as well
as to enable the whole family to avoid starvation".

In view of the above, I hereby write you this letter,
with the request that you will allow the said Chiang Vung
Kwei to be released upon furnishing shop security.

I remain,

Yours faithfully,

Wang Lu Ngou,
Attorney-at-law.
2-8-38.

At 10.30 a.m., July 27, D.S. Hide, D.S.I. Rew
ren-ken and D.J. McKeown proceeded to Chengtu Road
Station and solicited assistance in effecting the
arrest of five persons connected with the "Thrift
Society" formed by employees of the Commercial Press.
Assistance was rendered by D.S. Dockson and resulted in
the arrest of three persons namely :
(1) Tsang Bei-njoeh (張培鈺), monotype
setter, residing at 133 Nansuh Road.
(2) Zia Fon-sung (謝福生), apprentice
in the photographic department, residing
at Lane 552, No.19 Hart Road.
(3) Tsih Jing-tuh (戚信德), apprentice in
the paper plate department, residing in
Room 54, Chungsan Lodging House, 480
Tientsin Road.
The total of persons ■■ in custody is now
sixteen.
The homes of the persons arrested on July 27
were searched but nothing of an incriminating nature
was found. Statements were taken from them and from
the four persons arrested on the afternoon of July 26.
All are attached to this report. Regarding the other
two persons who are wanted in connection with this case,
namely Kuh Ngoeh-loong (葛玉龍) and Ling Tsoong-zai
(林鐘才), Kuh Ngoeh-loong is on sick leave and his
home address is unknown. There is a possibility that
he has gone into hiding. Regarding Ling Tsoong-zai,

7月27日上午10时30分，D.S. Hide、侦探副督察 Rew ren-ken（原文不清）和 D.J. McKeown 前往成都路捕房，寻求协助逮捕五名与商务印书馆员工组成的“节约社”有关的人员。D.S. Dockson 提供了协助，结果逮捕了三名人员，即：

(15) Tsang Sei-ngoen (張培銀): Assisted in the formation of the "After Office Hours Reading Society", an organization of a national salvation nature. Admits being a member of the "Thrift Society."

(16) Zia Fon-sung (謝福生): Denies that he consented to join the society. Can give no reason for his name being included in the list of members found in the minute book of the meetings.

Lists of literature seized from various accused
arrested after July 24 are attached as an appendix.
Further efforts will be made to effect the
arrest of Ling Tsong-zai andruh Seok-leong, the
only two persons wanted who are now at large.
It is apparent that the "Thrift Movement"
has suffered a setback in its infancy. Although it
does not appear to be a dangerous movement on the
surface, being concerned with avoiding unnecessary
expenses, the procedure of investigating shops dealing
in Japanese and other foreign goods would undoubtedly
lead to grave abuses. There appears to be an opinion
that the movement is sponsored by the Peoples Political
Council of the Chinese Republic, but it is now clear that
a communist element is taking advantage of the situation,
and may be well able to sway the local populace under the
guise of patriotism. The management appears to be on
the side of the workers. Although, when first approached,
they promised to cooperate fully with the Police in this
case, and undoubtedly did render considerable assistance,
their attitude has now changed and they are inclined to
frown on Police action, making further progress in the
discovery of radical elements among the workers
problematical. According to one report from within the
factory, all workers have been instructed to destroy all
incriminating documents in their possession which
possibly explains the reason for no literature being

将进一步努力逮捕凌宗宰 (Ling Tsong-zai) 和陆锡良 (ruh Seok-leong)，此二人为目前仍在逃的唯一两名通缉人员。
显然，“节约运动”在萌芽阶段遭受了挫折。虽然从表面看，该运动关注避免不必要的开支，似乎并非危险运动，但调查销售日货及其他外国商品的商店的程序无疑会导致严重的滥用行为。有一种观点认为该运动由中华民国国民参政会赞助，但现在清楚的是，共产党分子正在利用这一局势，并很可能以爱国为幌子煽动当地民众。管理层似乎站在工人一边。虽然起初他们承诺在此案中全力配合警方，且确实提供了相当多的协助，但其态度现已改变，倾向于对警方行动表示不满，使得在工人中发现激进分子的进一步进展变得困难。根据工厂内部的一份报告，所有工人都已接到指示销毁其持有的所有罪证文件，这或许解释了为何在7月27日

The following is the statement of Ching Tsang Zai (金掌才)

My name is Ching Tsai-zai. I am 21 years old,
a native of Pootung, and single. I reside in Lane 172,
2 Avenue Joffre. I have worked in the type-setting
Room of the Commercial Press, Lane 688, No.694 Bubbling
Road, for three years.
I received my education in the Kwang Dz An
(廣慈院) Primary School, Minghong.
I am a member of the Commercial Press Employees'
Mutual Aid Society, which is without an office.
At the request of Tsang Tseng-ming (張振民)
(in custody), I agreed to join the "Thrift" Movement.
I have not attended the secret meetings in the Chien
Chwang Middle School, 318 Weihaiwei Road, nor have I
done anything in the movement.
As to the secret anti-Japanese publications
entitled the "Unity" and "Long Hwa" (Wave), which were
seized by the Municipal Police at my house on July 26,
they were given me by Chiang Wei-kwei (蔣文桂)
(in custody) in the factory at Lane 688, No.694 Bubbling
Well Road, free of charge, during the past four months.
I cannot give any reason for Chiang passing the magazines
to me rather than to any other of the workers in the
Commercial Press.

(Signed): Ching Tsang-zai.

My name is Soong nsi-vung. I am 28 years old,
a native of Tsungming and married. I reside at 119 Rue
Chapei. I have been a worker in the tin plate making
room of the Commercial Press, Lane 688, No. 694 Bubbling
Well Road, for ten years.
I received my education in the Pootung Primary
School, Tsungming Island, and in the Commercial Press
Supplementary School, Paoshan Road, Chapei.
I am a member of the "Thrift" Movement. I
attended two secret meetings bearing on the movement on
June 30 (1st meeting) and July 10 (2nd meeting) in the
Chien Chwang Middle School, 318 Weihaiwei Road. I was
asked to join the movement by Tsang Tseng-ming (in custody).
About four or five days prior to the 1st meeting
(June 30), Tsang Tseng-ming gave me a draft of a handbill
bearing on the "Thrift" Movement for perusal and suggested
that it should be copied and the copies could be given to
others. I thereupon stated that I could arrange for the
printing free of charge. He gave me the draft which I
later handed to Tsih Sing-tuh ( 戚信德 ) (in custody)
for the necessary arrangements for printing. Altogether
about 60 copies were printed which when completed, I
handed to Tsang Tseng-ming. I do not know where it was
printed as the printing was arranged by Tsih Sing-tuh
nor do I have any knowledge of the disposal of the 60
copies by Tsang Tseng-ming.
I am a member of the Commercial Press Employees'

The following is the statement of Chang ruh-hwa (張德華)
native of Canton taken by me D.S. McKeown
at Chengtu Rd Stn on the 27/7/38 and interpreted by Clerk Loh Wei-kong

My name is Chang ruh-hwa, aged 21, native of
Canton, single, residing at 27 Sung Ping Li, rue de
Saigon. I was educated at the Sze Pon (市北)
Middle School, Chapei. I have been an apprentice for
five years in the photography department of the
Commercial Press for five years. About two weeks ago,
Chiang Wen-kwei (文桂) approached me and
requested me to join the "Thrift Society". I thought
that the society was of a political nature and was
reluctant to join. Outwardly I consented to join
because I was afraid but I did not attend the meetings
although I was told to attend on two occasions. As to
the two copies of the "Long hwa" (Wave), a national
salvation periodical found in my room, they were give
to me by Chiang Jen kwei two months ago to read.

(Signed): Chang ruh-hwa.

本人名叫张德华，21 岁，广东人，未婚，住西贡路（rue de Saigon）宋平里 27 号。本人曾就读于闸北市北中学。本人在商务印书馆摄影部当学徒已五年。约两周前，蒋文桂（Chiang Wen-kwei）找上我，要求我加入“节约社”。我认为该社团具有政治性质，不愿加入。表面上我因害怕而同意加入，但我并未参加会议，尽管曾两次被告知要出席。至于在我房间内发现的两份救国期刊《龙华》（Long hwa，即《浪花》），是两个月前蒋仁桂（Chiang Jen kwei）给我阅读的。

My name is Koo Ling-sung, aged 20, native of
Soochow, married, residing at No.61 Shao yue Li, Zicawei.
I was educated at the No.1 Commercial Knowledge
Supplementary School, Boone Road. I have been an
apprentice in the Glass Department of the Commercial
Press for two years. About two weeks ago Tsang Tseng
Ming (張增明) requested me to join the "Thrift Society"
and told me that secret meetings would be held every two
weeks in the Chien Chwang Middle School, Weihaiwei Road.
I consented to join. I have not attended the meetings
because I was otherwise engaged. I became acquainted
with Tsang Tseng Ming during the course of business.
Tsang Tseng Ming told me that the object of the movement
was to be thrifty. If this was the only object of the
Society, I do not know why the meetings should be held
in secret. I do not know who seconded my membership.

(Signed): Koo Ling-sung.

本人名叫顾林生，20 岁，苏州人，已婚，住徐家汇绍悦里 61 号。本人曾就读于布恩路（Boone Road）第一商业补习学校。本人在商务印书馆玻璃部当学徒已两年。约两周前，张增明（Tsang Tseng Ming）要求我加入“节约社”，并告诉我每两周在威海卫路建章中学举行秘密会议。我同意加入。我因另有事务而未出席会议。我是在业务往来中结识张增明的。张增明告诉我，该运动的目标是节约。如果这是该社唯一的目标，我不明白为何会议要秘密举行。我不知道是谁介绍我入会的。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.
The following is the statement of Tsih Sing-tun (戚信德)
native of Yuyao taken by me D. J. McKeown
at Chengtu Rd Stn. on the 27/7/38 and interpreted by D.S.I. Rao Yen-ken

My name is Tsih Sing-tuh. I am 21 years old,
a native of Yuyao, Chekiang, and single. I reside in
Room 54, Chungsan Lodging House, 480 Tientsin Road,
where I have stayed since July 23 (one day before the
raid on the Chien Chwang School, Weihaiwei Road).
I have worked as an apprentice in the Paper Plate Room
of the Commercial Press, Lane 638, No.694 Bubbling Well
Road, for two years.

I received my education in the Tsing Sing
(清心) Primary School, Great South Gate, Nantao.
Towards the end of June, Tsang Tseng-ming
(張振民) (in custody) advised me to join the "Thrift
Movement." I attended a secret meeting in the Chien
Chwang Middle School, 318 Weihaiwei Road, on July 10.
The movement is aimed at thrift and refraining from
using Japanese products.

During the meeting, Wong Ching-san (王金山)
(in custody) reported that he had unknowingly purchased a
pair of trousers from the A.I.C. Underwear Co., Nanking
Road, of Japanese origin, and advised us not to buy goods
from the A.B.C. Company

Towards the end of June, Tsang Tseng-ming gave
Soong Hsi-weng (宋希文) (in custody) a draft of a
handbill bearing on the movement for perusal in the
factory. As Soong suggested that it should be printed
instead of being copied, I at that time was by their side
and volunteered to arrange for the printing free of charge.

以下为戚信德（Tsih Sing-tun，余姚籍）的供词，由本人 D. J. McKeown 于 1938 年 7 月 27 日在成都路捕房录取，并由高级巡官 Rao Yen-ken 传译。

本人名叫戚信德（Tsih Sing-tuh）。本人 21 岁，浙江余姚人，未婚。本人住在天津路 480 号中山旅舍 54 室，自 7 月 23 日（即威海卫路建章中学遭搜查的前一天）起一直居住于此。本人在静安寺路（Bubbling Well Road）694 号 638 弄商务印书馆纸盘部当学徒已两年。

本人曾在南市大南门清心小学受教育。6 月底，张振民（Tsang Tseng-ming，在押）劝我加入“节约运动”。7 月 10 日，我参加了在威海卫路 318 号建章中学举行的秘密会议。该运动旨在节约并抵制日货。

会议期间，王金山（Wong Ching-san，在押）报告说，他无意中在南京路 A.I.C. 内衣公司购买了一条日本制造的裤子，并建议我们不要从 A.B.C. 公司购买商品。

6 月底，张振民给宋希文（Soong Hsi-weng，在押）一份关于该运动的传单草稿，让其在工厂内传阅。由于宋希文建议将其印刷而非抄写，我当时在他们身边，自愿安排免费印刷。

The following is the statement of Tsang Bei-ngoeh (莊培鈺)
native of Ningpo taken by me D.S. McKeown
at Chengtu Rd Stn on the 27/7/38 and interpreted by Clerk Loh Wei-kong.

Tsang Bei-ngoeh, age 32, native of Ningpo.
I am married, residing at 133 Nansuh Road. I have been
a monotype-setter of the Printing Department of the
Commercial Press for seventeen years.
In April, 1938, Soong Hsi-wen solicited my opinion
in connection with the proposed formation of a "Society
to Study After Working Period" (業餘讀書會).
I agreed, but the "society" has not yet come into existence.
About three weeks ago, while working in the factory,
Lane 688, No.694 Bubbling Well Road, Soong Hsi-wen requested
me to participate in the "Thrift Movement." I consented.
On July 23, Soong Hsi-wen told me to attend the
meeting which was held at the Chien Chwang Middle School,
Weihaiwei Road. I attended the meeting between 8 a.m.
and 11 a.m. July 24 when some eight persons including
Soong Hsi-wen were present. During this meeting it was
discussed and agreed not to use the goods of the A.B.C.
Underwear Company, Nanking Road, the Yah Dah Ziang
(協大祥) Cotton Cloth Shop (French Concession)
and of the "Hazelwood," as they are reported to be dealing

庄培鈺，32 岁，宁波人。
本人已婚，住南苏州路 133 号。本人在商务印书馆印刷部担任单字铸排机操作员已十七年。
1938 年 4 月，宋希文就拟议成立“业余读书会”一事征求我的意见。我表示同意，但该“会”尚未成立。约三周前，当本人在静安寺路 694 号 688 弄的工厂工作时，宋希文要求我参加“节约运动”。我同意了。7 月 23 日，宋希文让我参加在威海卫路建章中学举行的会议。我在 7 月 24 日上午 8 点至 11 点之间参加了会议，当时包括宋希文在内约有八人出席。在这次会议上，大家讨论并同意不使用南京路 A.B.C. 内衣公司、法租界协大祥棉布店以及“Hazelwood”（音译）的商品，因为据称这些商家经销日货。此后我再未参加任何会议。
本人从未参与任何政治活动，也不是任何政治组织的成员。

（签名）：庄培鈺。

FORM 4
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.
The following is the statement of Zai Foh-sung (謝福生)
native of ruyao, Chekiang taken by me D.S. McKeown
at Chengtu Rd Stn on the 27/7/38 and interpreted by Clerk Loh Wei-kong.

My name is Zai Foh-sung, age 19, native of
ruyao, Chekiang. I am single, residing at Lane 552,
19 Hart Road. I received my education at the Orphan
Institute (孤兒院), Lunghwa. I have been an
apprentice at the Photography Department of the
Commercial Press for about two years.
About two months ago, Sung Yah-tsing (沈學進)
(in custody) approached me and asked me to join the
"Thrift Society." I objected as I do not support the
movement. Sung Yah-tsing made no further attempt to
induce me to join the movement until July 23, when he
and Wong Ching-san (王金山) (also in custody) told
me to attend a meeting at the Chien Chwang Middle School,
Weihaiwei Road on July 24. I rejected the suggestion
and did not attend the meeting.
I am at a loss to understand why my name was on
the list. I have never participated in movements of a
political nature.

本人名叫谢福生，19 岁，浙江 ruyao（原文不清，疑为余姚或瑞安）人。本人未婚，住哈同路（Hart Road）19 号 552 弄。本人曾在龙华孤儿院受教育。本人在商务印书馆摄影部当学徒约两年。
约两个月前，沈学进（Sung Yah-tsing，在押）找我，要求我加入“节约社”。我因不支持该运动而拒绝。沈学进未再试图劝诱我加入，直到 7 月 23 日，他和王金山（Wong Ching-san，亦在押）让我于 7 月 24 日参加在威海卫路建章中学举行的会议。我拒绝了该建议，并未出席会议。
我不明白为何我的名字会在名单上。我从未参与过具有政治性质的运动。

REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Hsu Hai-keng (徐海根).
native of Wusih taken by me D.J. McKeown
at Chengtu Rd.Stn on the 25/7/38 and interpreted by D.S.I. Kao Yen-ken

My name is Hsu Hai-keng (徐海根). I am
19 years of age, a native of Wusih and single. I reside
in Lane 1, 34 Markham Road. I have been employed in the
Commercial Press as an apprentice in the Accounting
Department for one year.
I received my education in the Sam Yoeh Middle
School, Hung Tung Road, Chapei.
Following the outbreak of hostilities in August,
1937, I joined the Vocational Circles National Salvation
Association, Sin Kwan Primary School, Park Road (now
defunct). I was assigned to propaganda work among the
Commercial Press employees. At that time about 50
copies of the "Unity" were sent by the Vocational Circles
National Salvation Association to Chang Mei (张勉), an
employee of the Accounting Department of the Commercial
Press (now transferred to Hongkong), who in turn gave
the copies to me for distribution among the Commercial
Press employees.
In March, 1938, he was transferred to the
Hongkong Office of the Commercial Press, since when 50
copies per issue have been sent to me to the Head Office
of the Commercial Press direct. Of these copies, I sent
15 copies to Chiang Wen-kwei (蒋文桂) and I distributed
14 copies among the employees of the Accounting Department,
and the remainder to those employees on the 3rd floor
(Printing Matter Order Section) and those on the ground
floor. The man who sends the copies to me is named Woo.

以下是由我，D.J. McKeown，于1938年7月25日在成都路巡捕房对无锡籍人士徐海根（Hsu Hai-keng）进行的讯问记录，由督察长高恩坚（Kao Yen-ken）翻译。

我叫徐海根（Hsu Hai-keng）。我今年19岁，无锡人，未婚。我居住在马克姆路34号1弄。我在商务印书馆会计部担任学徒已有一年。
我就读于闸北鸿通路三友中学（Sam Yoeh Middle School）。
1937年8月战事爆发后，我加入了职业界救国会，该会位于公园路新关小学（现已解散）。我被指派在商务印书馆员工中进行宣传工作。当时，职业界救国会向商务印书馆会计部员工张勉（Chang Mei，现已调往香港）寄送了约50本《团结》，张勉随即将这些刊物交给我，以便在商务印书馆员工中分发。
1938年3月，他调往商务印书馆香港办事处，此后每期50本刊物直接寄至商务印书馆总馆给我。在这些刊物中，我寄给蒋文桂（Chiang Wen-kwei）15本，将其余14本分发给会计部员工，剩下的分发给三楼（印刷品订单科）和一楼的员工。给我寄送刊物的人名叫伍（Woo）。

About 3 months ago, one Jong Chun (    ) was the
messenger. I do not know the whereabouts of either Jong
Chun or Woo. No subscription fees are charged for the
magazines but contributions are solicited. About one
month ago I handed Woo contributions ranging from $0.30
to $2.10 on two occasions. This money I collected from
various employees in the Head Office. I have not received
the "Unity" for one month. I do not know why.

Chiang Jen-kwei became a member of the now
defunct Vocational Circles National Salvation Association
following the hostilities in August, 1937. In the
association, Chiang and I became well acquainted. About
three months ago Chiang gave me five copies of the "Long
Hwa" (Wave) (a secret publication of an anti-Japanese
nature), and later 5 copies each on two other occasions.
I know that Chiang formed an organization named "Yuin Zoe "
(行社) which is responsible for the publication of
"Long Hwa". At his request I attended a meeting for a
discussion of current affairs, social science and the
national salvation movement which was held at his house,
Vee Teh Primary School, Kuo Tsao Li, Sinza Road, about
two months ago and which was attended by some ten persons.
I know only Chiang while those others present were students
and workers of the Commercial Press unknown to me.

I am not a member of the "Thrift" Movement, nor
have I joined the Chinese Communist Party.

蒋仁贵（Chiang Jen-kwei）在1937年8月战事后成为了现已解散的职业界救国会成员。在该会中，蒋和我变得熟识。大约三个月前，蒋给了我五本《浪花》（Long Hwa）（一种具有反日性质的秘密出版物），后来又在另外两次场合各给了我5本。我知道蒋成立了一个名为“行社”（Yuin Zoe）的组织，负责出版《浪花》。应他的要求，我参加了大约两个月前在他家中举行的时事、社会科学和救国运动讨论会，地点在新闸路郭灶里维德小学（Vee Teh Primary School），约有十人参加。我只认识蒋，其他在场者是我并不认识的商务印书馆的学生和工人。

我不是“节约”运动的成员，也没有加入中国共产党。

at present located at 694 Bubbling Well Road, well known
in the past for the truculent and subversive attitude
of its employees. The school in which the meeting was
held namely the Chien Chwang Middle School was moved from

of a staff member of the school named Woo Zing (吳靖)
alias Woo Vung Ping (吳文賓) who was fully cognizant of

him during the afternoon of July 24, and he was taken
into custody at 5.45 p.m. He is also detained as Zung
Pau Zien stated that Woo Vung Ping knew the purpose of
the meeting. The arrest of Chiang Wen-kwei appears to
be an important one. Although he strongly denies being a
communist and explains his position by stating that he
had recently been requested to join the Communist Party

The following is the statement of Shih Hsien-wei (施賢威)
native of Asin taken by me D.S. Meredith.
at Chengtu Rd. Str. on the 24/7/38 and interpreted by D.S.J. Kao Yen-sen.

My name is Shih Hsien-wei. I am 22 years old,
a native of Asin, and single. I reside at Lane 750,
Sincza Road. I have been employed as a clerk in the
General Affairs Department of the Commercial Press,
694 Bubbling Well Road, for about 6 years.
I received my education in the San Yoch (三育)
Middle School, Hong Tung Road (恆通路), Shanghai.
Following the outbreak of hostilities in August,
1937, my school mate named Huang Yang-shi (黃養熙) who
is an employee of the China Aviation Corporation, then in
Shanghai but now at Hankow, came to me and advised me to
take part in the national salvation movement. Meanwhile he
gave me a number of novels of a leftist nature for reading
and later comments on the anti-Japanese campaign and finally
on socialism. Huang was then a member of the now defunct
Cultural Circles National Salvation Association and was
connected with the Chinese Communist Party. In October,
1937, he left for Hankow with the Corporation. He often
writes to me and recommends me publications to be perused.
After reading a large number of leftist books, I began to worship
worship the Communist doctrine.
About a month ago, Huang wrote to me, introducing
to me one Yang (楊) who, Huang alleged, was an excellent
leftist (Communist) and whom I could approach on socialistic
ideas. In the letter, he asked me to meet Yang at the front
gate of the French Park, corner of Rue Lafayette and
Avenue Dubail at 6 p.m. on a Wednesday; I cannot recollect

以下是施贤威（Shih Hsien-wei）的供词，籍贯亚新（Asin），由我，侦探副督察梅雷迪思（D.S. Meredith），于1938年7月24日在成都路捕房录取，并由侦探副督察高延森（D.S.J. Kao Yen-sen）翻译。

我叫施贤威。今年22岁，籍贯亚新（Asin），未婚。我住在新闸路750弄。我在静安寺路694号商务印书馆总务部担任职员约6年。
我在上海恒通路的三育中学接受教育。
1937年8月战事爆发后，我的同学黄养熙（Huang Yang-shi）来找我，劝我参加救国运动。他当时是中国航空公司的雇员，身在上海，现居汉口。期间，他给我一些左翼性质的小说阅读，后来是关于抗日运动的评论，最后是关于社会主义的内容。黄当时是现已解散的文化界救亡协会的成员，并与中国共产党有联系。1937年10月，他随公司前往汉口。他经常写信给我，推荐刊物供我阅读。在阅读了大量左翼书籍后，我开始崇拜共产主义学说。
大约一个月前，黄写信给我，向我介绍了一位姓杨（Yang）的人，黄声称此人是一位优秀的左翼分子（共产党员），我可以就社会主义思想与其接触。信中要求我在某个星期三下午6点，在法租界公园（French Park）正门，即辣斐德路（Rue Lafayette）与杜美路（Avenue Dubail）转角处与杨会面；我记不清

A friend of Huang Yang-shi, each time 10 copies are sent
to me. He is a Communist and he does not let me know his
address. I know that it is printed in Shanghai, but
I have no idea as to the printing place. I distributed
them among the fellow workers of the Commercial Press.
Contribution fees were charged & volunteer subscriptions
were solicited. In all I remitted subscriptions ranging
from $0.50 to $4.50 on four different occasions to him.

I have also received copies of the secret publica-
tions entitled the "Unity" (團結) since January, 1938.
For each issue, I received 15 copies. Five of them I
gave to Chang Tseng-ming (in custody) (張振), five to
other fellow-workers including Tien Tsai-sai (田瑞少),
three to my friends named Wong Han-ping (王涵萍), a
telephone operator of the Texaco, 12 The Bund, and two for myself
and my brother. These books are given me by Hsu Hai-keng
(徐海根), an apprentice of the Accounting Department
of the Commercial Press Head Office, Honan Road, free of
charge. They are delivered to me at the Commercial Press
factory on Bubbling Well Road by Hsu with the assistance of
messengers of the Commercial Press.

About two months ago I attempted to push the
national salvation movement among my friends. I intended to
form an "After Office Hours" Reading Society but without
success owing to lack of suitable place. The following
persons I approached agreed to join the movement:-
Wong Yu-ping (王涵萍), Texaco Co., 12 The Bund.

大约两个月前，我试图在朋友中推动救国运动。我打算成立一个“业余”读书会，但因缺乏合适的场所而未成功。我接洽的以下人员同意加入该运动：-

I am 25 years old, a native of Shun h i Sze le.
I reside at 157 East Sze Wen Li (東斯文里), Sincere Road.
I have been employed in the Commercial Press, Tung Ho Li
(同和里 Lane 694), publishing well known, as a photo engraver,
for two years.

I was educated in the Tsien Tso (颛桥) Primary
school, Tsie cho, near it on.

Towards the end of June, 193, Chian Wen-kwei
(蔣文桂) and Chang Sen-min (張振民) (in custody)
promoted a "thrift" movement. They advised Sun Yuh-tsin
(沈学進), Sun Fan-zien (陈济全) etc to join the
movement. He agreed. They explained to us that in the
movement, we should refrain from purchasing Japanese
products and further that we should use few foreign products
so as to prevent money from going abroad.

On June 29 Sun Yuh-tsin gave me a printed copy of
a handbill bearing on the "thrift" movement, saying that
he obtained it from Chang Sen-min.

I attended three meetings in the Chien Chwang (泉漳)
Middle School, 318 Weihaiwei Road, on June 30, July 10 and
July 24. Although we decided to investigate the firms
dealing in Japanese products and extend the movement to
the public, yet we have not done so.

At the second meeting (on July 10), I made a report
that I had bought a pair of khaki trousers from the A.B.C.
Underwear Co., Nanking Road, near Fokien Road, and according
to a friend of mine named Loh Yung-kong (陳永康), a

我今年25岁，籍贯顺德四会（Shun h i Sze le，原文拼写可能有误，通常指广东顺德）。我住在新闸路东斯文里157号。我在同和里（Lane 694）著名的出版机构商务印书馆担任照相制版师已有两年。

我在颛桥（Tsien Tso）小学接受教育，位于颛桥附近。

1938年6月底，蒋文桂（Chian Wen-kwei）和张振民（Chang Sen-min）（在押）发起了一场“节约”运动。他们劝沈学进（Sun Yuh-tsin）、陈济全（Sun Fan-zien，注：中文名与拼音不符，依拼音可能为孙范先等，但此处依原文括号内中文译出）等人加入该运动。他同意了。他们向我们解释，在该运动中，我们应避免购买日本产品，此外还应少用外国产品，以防止资金外流。

6月29日，沈学进给了我一份关于“节约”运动的印刷传单，说是从张振民那里得到的。

我参加了6月30日、7月10日和7月24日在威海卫路318号泉漳中学举行的三次会议。虽然我们决定调查经营日货的公司并将运动推广至公众，但我们尚未这样做。

The following is the statement of Sung Yeu Jsing (沈學進) age 22.
native of Nanzing taken by me D.S. McKeown
at Chengtu Rd Stn. on the 24/7/38. and interpreted by D.J.I. Kao Yen Ken.

My name is Sung Yeu Jsing (沈學進), aged 22, single,
native of Nanzing. I was educated at the Zong Kung Primary
School, Paoshan Road, Chapei. I reside at No. 12, Yen Zung
Li, Tsepoo Road. I have been employed in the Commercial
Press, 694 Bubbling Well Road as a colour photographer for
four years.

About six weeks ago, one named Tsang Tseng King (張振卿)
who is also an employee of the Commercial Press approached me
and suggested that I should become a member of the "Thrift
Movement, which was being inaugurated for the purpose of pro-
moting thrift among all classes of Chinese and to advocate a
boycott against Japanese goods. I have attended three meetings
in the Chien Chwang Middle School, 328 Weihaiwei Road on June
30th, July 10th and 24th. Although in the first meeting we
decided to investigate the location of shops selling enemy
goods, we have not yet done so, because we have not had time.
According to one resolution, each member had to introduce a
new member within two weeks. I was to introduce one named Tseu
Kung Zee (周根泉), a fellow worker but he failed to attend the
meeting today.

我叫沈学进（Sung Yeu Jsing），22岁，未婚，南京籍。我曾就读于闸北宝山路宗公小学。我住在新闸路延庆里12号。我在静安寺路694号商务印书馆担任彩色摄影师已有四年。

大约六周前，一名同样受雇于商务印书馆的名为张振卿（Tsang Tseng King）的人接近我，建议我加入“节约运动”，该运动旨在促进各阶层中国人的节约风气，并倡导抵制日货。我参加了6月30日、7月10日和24日在威海卫路328号健庄中学举行的三次会议。虽然在第一次会议上我们决定调查销售敌货的商店位置，但我们尚未这样做，因为我们没有时间。根据一项决议，每位成员必须在两周内介绍一名新成员。我本应介绍一位名叫周根泉（Tseu Kung Zee）的同事，但他未能参加今天的会议。

My name is Zung Pau Zien ( ) I am aged 24
and a native of Ningpo and married. I reside at No. 8a Shanse
Road. I have been employed in the Commercial Press, 694 Bubbling
Well Road, as a typesetter for about 3 years. I was educated
in the Shang Tuh (尚德.) Primary School, Deh Chih Road, Nan-
tao. I am a member of the Commercial Press Employees Mutual Aid
Union, which is a secret organization without an office.
About 4 weeks ago, Chiang Wen-kwei and Tsang Tseng-ming
( in custody) came to me in the Commercial Press Factory and
discussed with me the "Thrift Movement". They showed me an arti-
cle in the China Press stating that the movement had been started
in Hankow. They mentioned that about 10 workers of the Commer-
cial Press had joined and asked me whether I could find a place
where they could meet and discuss the movement. I therefore
arranged for the leasing of the Chien Chwang Middle School on
Weihaiwei Road as the meeting place. I know a staff employee of
the school named Woo Wen-ping (吳文賓) and I explained to him
the nature of the meeting. Altogether three meetings were held
there namely on June 30, July 10 and July 20. I attended all the
meetings. At the first meeting we decided to investigate the
shops dealing with enemy goods and to extend the movement to the
public, starting with fellow-workers and relatives. So far we
have not made any investigations. At the second meeting on July
10th, Wong Ching Say (王金山 in custody) reported that he had
bought a pair of khaki trousers from the A.B.C. Company, Nanking
Road, near Hokien Road and that he had ascertained from his friend
that the shop was dealing in Japanese goods. He therefore asked

The following is the statement of Tsang Tseng Ming (張振民).
native of Tsungming taken by me D.J. McKeown
at Chengtu Rd Stn. on the 24/7/38. and interpreted by D.S.I. Kao Yen Ken

My name is Tsang Tseng Ming (張振民). I am 19 years old, a native of Tsungming and single. I reside in the Da Dzu Refugee Camp, 540 Ningpo Road. My family live at 152 Rue Chapsal. I have been employed as an apprentice to proof-readers in the Commercial Press, Tung Wu Li, Bubbling Well Road for about 3 years.

I received my education in the Ming Peng (民本) Middle School, Tsungming.

Following the outbreak of hostilities in August, 1937, I was thrown out of employment and went to serve in the Heng Zung Refugee Camp (now closed), corner of Tientsin and Kiangse Roads, and later in the Da Dzu Refugee Camp, 540 Ningpo Road, as an accountant. I returned to work in the Commercial Press at the end of February, 1938.

Towards the end of June, 1938, Chiang Wen-kwei (蔣文桂) (in custody) and I discussed an article in the Chinese press stating that a "Thrift Movement" was in progress in Hankow and inland places. We decided to promote the movement and therefore invited
(1) Wang Ching San ( in custody)
(2) Zung Pau-zien ( in custody)
(3) Sung Yah-ching ( in custody)
(4) Soong Shi-wen ( not in custody)
and (5) Ling Tsoong-zai ( not in custody) to discuss the matter in the Chien Chwang Middle School, 318 Weihaiwei Road on June 30, when we laid down some rules of the movement and decided to investigate the firms dealing in Japanese goods and to extend the movement to the public. On the following day Soong Shi-wen (宋希文), a worker in the tin plate making room of the

以下为张振民（Tsang Tseng Ming）的陈述，崇明籍，由本人 D.J. McKeown 于1938年7月24日在成都路站讯问，并由 D.S.I. Kao Yen Ken 翻译。

我叫张振民（Tsang Tseng Ming）。我19岁，崇明籍，未婚。我住在宁波路540号的大慈难民收容所。我的家人住在霞飞路152号。我在静安寺路同裕里的商务印书馆担任校对学徒约3年。

我就读于崇明民本中学。

1937年8月战事爆发后，我失业了，先后在天津路与江西路转角处的恒众难民收容所（现已关闭）以及宁波路540号的大慈难民收容所担任会计。我于1938年2月底回到商务印书馆工作。

1938年6月下旬，蒋文桂（在押）和我讨论了中文报刊上的一篇文章，文章称汉口及内地正在进行“节约运动”。我们决定推广该运动，因此邀请了
(1) 王金山（在押）
(2) 陈沛全（在押）
(3) 沈学进（在押）
(4) 宋希文（未在押）
以及 (5) 林钟才（未在押）于6月30日在威海卫路318号健庄中学讨论此事，当时我们制定了一些运动规则，并决定调查经营日货的商号，并将运动推广至公众。次日，商务印书馆制罐车间的一名工人宋希文

Commercial Press, volunteered to have the rules of the movement
printed. About a week later, Soong brought to me on Bubbling
Well Road near the Commercial Press about 40 copies of a handbill
bearing on the movement. I carried the copies to the Press and
distributed them among the six persons above-mentioned for dis-
semination among those who were willing to join the movement. I
do not know where Soong printed the handbill. We held two fur-
ther meetings in the Chien Hwang Middle School on July 10 and 14.
I attended all of them up to now, about 20 persons, mostly Commer-
cial Press workers attended.

We promoted the movement because we want to be thrifty
and on the other hand we should at least refrain from buying
Japanese goods as the duty of patriots.

In May, 1938, Chiang Wen-kwei gave me five copies of a
secret publication entitled "Unity" ( anti-Japanese and National
Salvation nature ) free of charge. Up to the present, he has
given me four issues. The latest issue I received from Chiang
about ten days ago. For each issue, I received four or five cop-
ies, which, after reading I gave to Sung Yah-ching, Zung Pau-zien
and Wong Ching-san(王金山).

Last Sunday, July 17, at 8.30 a.m. I attended Chiang
Wen-kwei's house at his request. There I met four others and we
had a meeting there under the auspices of a "Long Hwa" (Wave)
Readers' Society. (The publication is of a national salvation
nature.) A man unknown to me presided. We discussed the "People's
Political Council" at Hankow. This Council was formed by repre-
sentatives of people to discuss government affairs According to
Chiang, the "Long Hwa" periodical came from Hongkong and is a secret
publication.

以下为（2）之陈述，籍贯……，由本人……于……在……讯问，并由……翻译。

自愿印制运动规则。大约一周后，宋在静安寺路商务印书馆附近给了我约40份关于该运动的传单。我将这些传单带到印刷厂，分发给上述六人，以便在愿意加入该运动的人群中传播。我不知道宋在哪里印制了传单。我们于7月10日和14日在健庄中学又举行了两次会议。到目前为止我都参加了，约有20人出席，大多是商务印书馆的工人。

我们推广该运动是因为我们要节约，另一方面，作为爱国者的责任，我们至少应 refrain from buying（ refrain from buying 意为避免购买，此处依语境译为“避免购买”）日货。

1938年5月，蒋文桂免费给了我五份名为《团结》的秘密刊物（具有抗日和救国性质）。到目前为止，他已给了我四期。最新一期是我大约十天前从蒋那里收到的。每期我收到四五份，阅读后我给了沈学进、陈沛全和王金山。

上周日，7月17日上午8点30分，应蒋文桂的要求，我去了他家。在那里我遇到了另外四个人，我们在“龙华”读者社的主持下在那里开了一个会。（该出版物具有救国性质。）一个我不认识的人主持了会议。我们讨论了汉口的“国民参政会”。该委员会由人民代表组成，以讨论政府事务。据蒋称，《龙华》期刊来自香港，是一份秘密出版物。

以下为张润弟（Zang Zung Dee），21岁，上海籍人士的陈述，由本人 D.S. McKeown 于1938年7月24日在成都路站讯问，并由 D.S.I. Kao Yen len 翻译。

我叫张润弟，21岁，上海籍，未婚，住在法租界高乃当路（Rue Francis Garnier）建邨里50号。我曾就读于南市乔家浜交通部员工子弟学校。我在静安寺路694号商务印书馆担任排字工已有两年。上个月某天，陈沛全（在押）邀请我加入“节约运动”。我同意了，并参加了7月24日上午的会议。会议刚开始，警察就进来逮捕了我们。

The following is the statement of Wong Kyung Dau (王景陶)
native of Shanghai taken by me D.S. McKeown
at Chengtu Rd Stn on the 24/7/38. and interpreted by D.S.I. Lao Yen Ken.

My name is Wong Kyung Dau (王景陶), age 21, native
of Shanghai, married, residing at No. 345 Huh Teh Li, Rue
Bourgeat, French Concession. I graduated from the Cheng Tong
Middle School, 318A Weihaiwei Road this year and I am unem-
ployed. I have nothing to do with the "Thrift Movement". As
to the draft entitled "Our Duty after the Loss of Greater
Shanghai", in which it is maintained that wall papers should be
posted, because all the newspapers are under the control of the
Japanese and people should take part in National Salvation
works, which was found in my possession, this is an essay based
on my opinion. It is not connected with the National Salvation
Movement. In my house, there are ten copies of the "Unity" and
ten copies of the "Students Livelihood", both of which are
secret anti-Japanese publications. These books were delivered
to me gratis by school mates in the spring term of this year.
Nearly all the students have copies. I do not belong to any
Society or political party.

以下为王景陶（Wong Kyung Dau）的陈述，上海籍，由本人 D.S. McKeown 于1938年7月24日在成都路站讯问，并由 D.S.I. Lao Yen Ken 翻译。

我叫王景陶，21岁，上海籍，已婚，住在法租界蒲石路（Rue Bourgeat）胡德里345号。我今年毕业于威海卫路318A号的成通中学，目前失业。我与“节约运动”无关。至于在我身上发现的题为《大上海沦陷后的我们的责任》的草稿，其中主张张贴标语，因为所有报纸都受日本人控制，人们应参与救国工作，这是我基于个人观点写的一篇文章。它与救国运动无关。我家中有十份《团结》和十份《学生生活》，两者都是秘密的反日出版物。这些书是今年春季学期由同学免费送给我的。几乎所有学生都有副本。我不属于任何社团或政党。

A brief trans ation of documents seized from the person
of Wong Kyung Pau ( ) who was arrested at the Chien
Chwang Middle School at 328 Weihaiwei Road on 24/7/38.

Our Duty After the Loss of The Greater Shanghai.

Consequent to the fall of Greater Shanghai two
and a half months ago, the Chinese population in the Inter-
national Settlement have been deprived of their protection.
Notwithstanding the fact that they are constantly handicapped
by the present adverse circumstances, countless number of
our patriotic comrades have engaged themselves in the work of
propaganda in order to awaken the people still in their slumber
and to strengthen their self-confidence. It should be borne
in mind, however, that the effect of their efforts is very
limited; and it is the duty of every one of our intellectual
circles to work along the following lines:-

1) The posting of wall newspapers:- As the
local newspapers are at present under the con-
trol of the Japanese Authorities and therefore
not reliable, the importance of posting wall
newspapers should not be lost sight of.

2) Soliciting for relief funds for the refugees:
Huge number of refugees are suffering in our
midst. It is my earnest hope that every one of
us should solicit for funds for the allevia-
tion of their suffering.

3) Participation in the work of National Salvation
: It is not enough for us just to confine our-
selves to study in schools. With a view to
better realizing the position in which our
country now finds itself and to the improve-
ment of our knowledge, we should take part in
organizations to work for the salvation of our
country and people, and for the attainment of
final victory at the last moment.

1938年7月24日，在威海卫路328号建庄中学逮捕的黄景宝（Wong Kyung Pau）（音译）身上搜获文件的简要译文。

大上海沦陷后的我们的职责。

自从两个半月前大上海沦陷以来，公共租界内的中国居民已失去了保护。尽管他们不断受到当前不利环境的阻碍，但无数爱国同志仍投身于宣传工作，以唤醒仍在沉睡中的民众并增强他们的自信心。然而，必须铭记的是，他们的努力效果非常有限；因此，我们知识界的每一个人都有责任按以下方针开展工作：—

1) 张贴壁报：— 由于当地报纸目前受日本当局控制，因而不可靠，故不应忽视张贴壁报的重要性。

2) 为难民募集救济款：大量难民在我们中间受苦。我恳切希望我们每个人都应募集资金，以减轻他们的苦难。

3) 参与救国工作：仅仅局限于在学校读书是不够的。为了更好地认识我国目前所处的处境并增进我们的知识，我们应该参加各种组织，为拯救国家和人民以及最终取得最后胜利而努力。

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1. Paper slip bearing hand written slogans, including the following:-
(1) Support the War of Resistance.
(2) Mobilize workers in commercial circles to participate in the war of resistance.
(3) Accelerate the establishment of a commercial workers united front.
(4) Support the "Mutual Aid Society".
(5) Maintain the relationship with the Shanghai printing circles in the "labour movement".
(6) Support the unification of the "labour movement" in Shanghai.
(7) Support the "National Workers' Anti-Japanese General Association" (全國工抗總會) (in Hankow).
(8) Eradicate Chinese traitors.

2. Paper slip bearing the following inscription:-
(1) If we insist on following legal organization, there will be a struggle.
(2) Struggle means strike and bloodshed.
(3) Any dispute between labour and capital at the present juncture must be the work of the Trotskyists.
(4) The Communist Party should be renamed "Mutual Assistance Party," since co-operation between the Kuomintang and the Communist Party still needs strengthening.
(5) To organize the populace means to dissolve the existing known legal organizations and to participate in secret activities without any legal protection whatsoever.
(6) The so-called improvement of people's livelihood is taken to mean the abandonment of the strength of the masses and listening to the capitalists.
(7) The so-called zealous leader, full of a sense of righteousness, only proceeds to divide the united masses, refusing to acknowledge his mistakes.
(8) If we destroy our own fortresses we obey and follow the capitalists.
(These notes are vague and in some cases cannot be properly translated)

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1. 纸条一张，载有手写标语，包括以下内容：—
(1) 支持抗战。
(2) 动员商界工人参加抗战。
(3) 加速建立商界工人统一战线。
(4) 支持“互助社”。
(5) 保持与上海印刷界在“劳工运动”中的关系。
(6) 支持上海“劳工运动”的统一。
(7) 支持（汉口）“全国工抗总会”。
(8) 铲除汉奸。

2. 纸条一张，载有以下文字：—
(1) 如果我们坚持遵循合法组织，就会发生斗争。
(2) 斗争意味着罢工和流血。
(3) 目前劳资之间的任何纠纷必定是托洛茨基分子所为。
(4) 共产党应更名为“互助党”，因为国共合作仍需加强。
(5) 组织民众意味着解散现有的已知合法组织，并在没有任何法律保护的情况下参与秘密活动。
(6) 所谓改善民生被理解为放弃群众力量并听命于资本家。
(7) 所谓充满正义感的热心领导者，只会分裂团结的群众，拒绝承认自己的错误。
(8) 如果我们摧毁自己的堡垒，我们就顺从并追随资本家。

A brief trans ation of documents seized from the person
of Wong Kyung Pau ( ) who was arrested at the Chien
Chwang Middle School at 318 Weihaiwei Road on 24/7/38.

Our Duty After the Loss of The Greater Shanghai.

Consequent to the fall of Greater Shanghai two
and a half months ago, the Chinese population in the Inter-
national Settlement have been deprived of their protection.
Notwithstanding the fact that they are constantly handicapped
by the present adverse circumstances, countless number of
our patriotic comrades have engaged themselves in the work of
propaganda in order to awaken the people still in their slumber
and to strengthen their self-confidence. It should be borne
in mind, however, that the effect of their efforts is very
limited; and it is the duty of every one of our intellectual
circles to work along the following lines:-

1) The posting of wall newspapers:- As the
local newspapers are at present under the con-
trol of the Japanese Authorities and therefore
not reliable, the importance of posting wall
newspapers should not be lost sight of.

2) Soliciting for relief funds for the refugees:
Huge number of refugees are suffering in our
midst. It is my earnest hope that every one of
us should solicit for funds for the allevia-
tion of their suffering.

3) Participation in the work of National Salvation:
It is not enough for us just to confine our-
selves to study in schools. With a view to
better realizing the position in which our
country now finds itself and to the improve-
ment of our knowledge, we should take part in
organizations to work for the salvation of our
country and people, and for the attainment of
final victory at the last moment.

1938年7月24日在威海卫路318号泉漳中学被捕的王景保（Wong Kyung Pau，(音译)）身上查获文件的简要译文。

大上海沦陷后我们的责任。

鉴于两个半月前大上海的沦陷，公共租界内的中国居民已失去保护。尽管他们不断受到当前不利环境的阻碍，无数爱国同志仍投身于宣传工作，以唤醒仍在沉睡中的民众并增强其自信心。然而，必须铭记，他们的努力效果非常有限；因此，我们知识界的每一个人都有责任按以下方针开展工作：-

1) 张贴壁报：- 由于当地报纸目前受日本当局控制，因而不可靠，故不应忽视张贴壁报的重要性。

2) 为难民募集救济款：大量难民在我们中间受苦。我恳切希望我们每个人都应募集资金，以减轻他们的苦难。

3) 参与救国工作：仅局限于在学校学习是不够的。为了更好地认识国家目前的处境并增进我们的知识，我们应参加各类组织，为拯救国家和人民以及最终取得胜利而努力。

(印：AL PIM ... 23 JULY 1938 ... SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE)

Information has been received that a number of
adherents of the local national salvation movement, who are
mainly students and workers, are contemplating promoting a
"Thrift" movement in Shanghai. It has been decided to
hold a secret meeting in the Chien Chwang (泉漳) Middle
School, 318 Weihaiwei Road (Chengtu Road District) at 8.30 a.m.
July 24 to discuss various measures for the fostering of this
movement. About 50 people are expected to attend.
According to arrangements already made, those attending the
meeting are requested to gather in the vicinity of the school
between 8 a.m. and 8.30 a.m. and at the appointed time
they will be led to the school. During the meeting it is
the intention of the promoters to distribute copies of a
handbill bearing on the "Thrift" movement, a copy of which
has been obtained and a translation follows :- This
handbill does not mention the source of issue.
"Quickly get up and promote the "Thrift" Movement
We will always believe that "the final victory
"will be scored by us". We strongly believe that "the
"final victory must be ours". We, however, must under-
"stand that the final victory does not only depend on the
"military strength, but also on the degree of endurance of
"the people. Therefore it is most urgent and important
"to put into force this "Thrift" movement.
We must enforce the "Thrift" movement by dispensing
"with all unnecessary expenses and refraining from purchasing
""enemy" goods, which are being dumped on the local market.

Ta Kei Pao and other local newspapers :- 9 AUG. 1938 A.M.

LOCAL THRIFT MOVEMENT

As a response to the thrift movement promoted by the National Government, leaders of various local Chinese circles are starting a thrift movement. On August 8, they issued the following circular addressed to Chinese residents in this locality :-
"Since the commencement of the war of resistance of China, the Chinese people have been closely consolidated and been struggling with an undaunted spirit for a final victory. We, living in this isolated island, are suffering from the increased cost of living and a large number of refugees are sheltered in the Foreign Settlements in the most distressful condition. It is true that various local amusement resorts are doing business far better than before and that dance halls, theatres, tea rooms and cabarets are always overcrowded. This shows that people in this isolated island are lovers of luxury, giving no consideration to national affairs.
"Japan, the invading race, is exercising thrift. Can we, the invaded people, whose houses have been gutted or whose families have been lost, waste our money lavishly for meaningless amusement? Local Chinese residents should immediately exercise thrift in their clothing and food. The money thus saved should be contributed towards the fund for the relief of refugees."
page_data.zh:
《大公报》及其他本地报纸：- 1938年8月9日 上午

本地节约运动

为响应国民政府倡导的节约运动，上海各界华人领袖正发起一场节约运动。8月8日，他们向本地华人居民发布了如下通告：-
“自中国抗战爆发以来，中国人民紧密团结，以无畏的精神为最终胜利而奋斗。我们身处这座孤岛，深受生活成本上涨之苦，且大量难民栖身于租界内，处境极为困苦。诚然，本地各类娱乐场所的生意比以往更加兴隆，舞厅、剧院、茶室和夜总会总是人满为患。这表明这座孤岛的居民沉溺于奢华，不顾国家大事。
“日本作为侵略者，尚且在厉行节约。我们这些家园被毁、亲人离散的被侵略者，岂能将金钱挥霍于无意义的娱乐之中？本地华人居民应立即在衣食方面厉行节约。所节省之款项应捐作难民救济基金。”
